name: AuthForm
summary: The sign-in and sign-up forms, which are one component.

props.name: labels
props.description: Every string on screen. No defaults, in any language: a label the kit invented would ship English into an app that has none, and it would do it silently.

props.name: busy
props.description: Disables the controls and spins the submit button.

props.name: error
props.description: A failure to show above the submit button, already translated. A sentence rather than a key, because the kit cannot translate and `toAuthMessageKey` hands the caller a key precisely so the caller can.

props.name: validate
props.description: Returns one message per invalid field, or null when the values are good. Omitted, the form submits whatever is typed and lets the server decide — which is a legitimate choice, not a broken one. `fieldErrors` turns a Zod schema into this in one line.

name: AuthShell
summary: The frame every sign-in screen sits in.

name: BaseAccordion
summary: A list that opens one section at a time.

props.name: multiple
props.description: Allow several open at once. Off by default, which is what makes it an accordion.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Which heading the control sits inside. A heading, always — it is how a screen reader user moves between sections without opening any of them. The level is a prop because it depends on what is above it on the page, and getting it wrong breaks the outline.

name: BaseAlert
summary: A message the reader has to take in before carrying on.

props.name: assertive
props.description: Announce immediately, interrupting. For failures the reader must act on.

name: BaseAvatar
summary: The person, in the corner where the account lives.

props.name: name
props.description: Used for the initials and, failing a `label`, as the accessible name.

props.name: label
props.description: Overrides the accessible name. For "Your account" rather than a person's name.

name: BaseBadge
summary: A small standing label: a level, a state, a count.

name: BaseBreadcrumb
summary: Where this page sits, and the way back up.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the landmark.

name: BaseButton
summary: The kit's button, and — when asked — its link.

props.name: as
props.description: What to render. `button` unless this navigates.

props.name: size
props.description: `xs` is the action inside a prompt or a nudge, not on a page.

props.name: type
props.description: Ignored unless `as` is `button`.

props.name: icon
props.description: Square, sized to its icon, with no label beside it. **Pass `aria-label`.** An icon on its own has no accessible name, and a control a screen reader announces as "button" is not usable. Attributes fall through, so `aria-label` lands where it should — nothing here can check that you passed one, which is why it is said this loudly.

props.name: block
props.description: Fills its container. The ordinary case under a form.

props.name: to
props.description: For `as="router-link"`.

props.name: href
props.description: For `as="a"`.

props.name: pill
props.description: Fully rounded rather than card-cornered. Every install prompt, update prompt and nudge across the apps used the same pair — a filled pill to act and a quiet one to dismiss — and none of them could use this component, because it only knew one corner radius.

props.name: pressed
props.description: That this button is a switch, and whether it is on. Omit it and the button is an action. Pass it and the button becomes a toggle: `aria-pressed` is written, and the variants that have an "off" look — ghost, quiet, secondary — take a filled one when on. There were 18 of these hand-written across the three apps, every one a picker cell or a filter chip, and almost none of them said `aria-pressed` at all. A screen reader met a row of identical buttons with no way to know which was chosen.

name: BaseCard
summary: A surface with a border, and optionally a head and a foot.

props.name: padding
props.description: How much room the card gives its contents. This component shipped with `px-5 py-4` baked in and was then used by nobody, across three apps and thirty-five hand-written card surfaces — which used `p-3` six times, `p-4` six times, `p-5` five times and `p-1` four times, and not once the pair this insisted on. A card that fixes its padding cannot be reached for, which is the same mistake `PageContainer` made with its width and `size="sm"` made with its height. `none` is for a card that holds a list: the rows own the padding, and the dividers have to reach the border.

name: BaseCheckbox
summary: A single checkbox, with its label beside it.

props.name: size
props.description: `md` is a setting: a line the reader came here to change, in ink. `sm` is an aside — "remember me" under a sign-in form, "show the ones I have learned" above a list — quieter and tighter. The two are not a guess. Of the five hand-written checkboxes across the three consuming apps, four were the aside and one was the setting, and they differed in exactly these two ways.

name: BaseCombobox
summary: A field you type into to narrow a list, then choose from it.

props.name: emptyLabel
props.description: Shown when nothing matches. Already translated.

name: BaseDisclosure
summary: One section that opens and closes.

props.name: title
props.description: The question. Already translated. Optional only because the `title` slot is the other way to give one — pass exactly one of them. A disclosure with neither has a control nobody can read, which is why this is documented rather than defaulted to something.

props.name: headingLevel
props.description: Which heading the control sits inside. A heading, always — it is how a screen reader user moves between sections without opening any of them. The level depends on what is above it on the page, and getting it wrong breaks the outline.

name: BaseInput
summary: A number field's value is a number.

props.name: labelHidden
props.description: Hides the label visually but keeps it for assistive tech. For fields whose surrounding row already names them — dropping the label entirely would leave the input with no accessible name at all.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm` for a field inside a row rather than in a form of its own.

props.name: variant
props.description: `unstyled` keeps the wiring and drops the surface. The label, the generated id, `aria-describedby` and the error are what a field is; the border and the height are what it looks like. A search box inside a bordered row, a url field in an editor popover — those places were hand-writing the whole thing to avoid the appearance, and losing the wiring with it. The same reasoning as `BaseButton`'s `unstyled`, and the same test: a primitive is finished when the app can take its behaviour without its paint.

name: BaseMenu
summary: A list of actions behind one control.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the trigger. Required: the trigger is usually a glyph.

props.name: align
props.description: Which edge the panel lines up with.

name: BaseModal
summary: A dialog that arrives from nowhere.

props.name: title
props.description: Names the dialog for assistive tech. Required; an unnamed dialog is a box.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the close button.

props.name: tone
props.description: `alert` marks it as a decision that interrupts — `role="alertdialog"`, which a screen reader announces immediately rather than on arrival.

props.name: dismissible
props.description: Whether Escape and the backdrop close it. Off for a dialog that must be answered — but never off as a way of forcing a reader to a decision they have not been given the information for.

name: BasePagination
summary: Moving between pages of a list.

props.name: page
props.description: Current page, 1-based.

props.name: pages
props.description: How many there are.

props.name: siblings
props.description: How many numbers to show either side of the current one.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the landmark.

props.name: previousLabel
props.description: Names for the arrows, already translated. Required, because `‹` is a glyph and not a word: a screen reader reading the arrow announces nothing a person can act on.

name: BaseRadioGroup
summary: A set of radios, and the reason there is no `BaseRadio`.

props.name: options
props.type: readonly { value: string; label: string; disabled?: boolean | undefined }[]

name: BaseSelect
summary: A native `<select>`, wearing the kit's field.

props.name: options
props.type: readonly { value: T; label: string; disabled?: boolean | undefined }[]

props.name: placeholder
props.description: An unselectable first row, for a field with no sensible default. Disabled rather than merely empty: an empty option that can be chosen lets someone go back to having answered nothing, which no form wants.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm` for a select that filters or sorts rather than answers a form. Every hand-written select across the three consuming apps was this one.

props.name: variant
props.description: `unstyled` keeps the wiring and drops the surface. The label, the generated id, `aria-describedby` and the error are what a field is; the border and the height are what it looks like. A search box inside a bordered row, a url field in an editor popover — those places were hand-writing the whole thing to avoid the appearance, and losing the wiring with it. The same reasoning as `BaseButton`'s `unstyled`, and the same test: a primitive is finished when the app can take its behaviour without its paint.

name: BaseSheet
summary: Pins the sheet to the area the keyboard has left visible.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: Accessible name for the close button. A prop rather than a translation: a component that calls t() forces every consumer onto one i18n setup, and this is the package's only visible string.

name: BaseSlider
summary: A value picked from a range, where roughly right is the point.

props.name: format
props.description: Turns the number into something a person would say — "45 minutes", "₺12". Used for the visible readout and for `aria-valuetext`, so both say the same thing and neither is a bare number.

name: BaseSpinner
summary: Work in progress, with no idea how much is left.

props.name: label
props.description: What is being waited for. Already translated.

name: BaseSwitch
summary: A setting that takes effect the moment it is touched.

props.name: labelHidden
props.description: For a switch inside a row that already names it — it keeps its accessible name.

name: BaseTable
summary: Rows of data, with the parts a hand-written `<table>` leaves out.

props.name: caption
props.description: What this table is. Required — an unnamed table is a box of numbers.

props.name: captionHidden
props.description: Keeps the caption for assistive tech when the page already shows a heading.

props.name: rowKey
props.description: Which field identifies a row. Falls back to the index.

name: BaseTabs
summary: Sections of one page, one visible at a time.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the tablist.

name: BaseTextarea
summary: A multi-line field.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm` tightens the label and the spacing. It does **not** shrink the text: iOS zooms the viewport when it focuses a field under 16px and never zooms back, which is why both phone apps force 16px on form elements in their base layer.

props.name: variant
props.description: `unstyled` keeps the wiring and drops the surface. The label, the generated id, `aria-describedby` and the error are what a field is; the border and the height are what it looks like. A search box inside a bordered row, a url field in an editor popover — those places were hand-writing the whole thing to avoid the appearance, and losing the wiring with it. The same reasoning as `BaseButton`'s `unstyled`, and the same test: a primitive is finished when the app can take its behaviour without its paint.

name: BaseTooltip
summary: A short label that appears beside a control.

props.name: label
props.description: The description. Already translated.

name: EmptyState
summary: A list with nothing in it yet, said kindly.

name: ErrorBoundary
summary: Keeps one broken screen from taking the whole app down.

props.name: resetKey
props.description: Clears the error whenever it changes — a route path, usually. An error on one screen should not follow somebody to the next one, and without this the boundary stays broken until a full reload.

name: FabButton
summary: The one action the app is built around, reachable from every screen.

props.name: label
props.description: The words beside the icon.

name: FormField
summary: A label, a hint, an error, and the wiring between them.

props.name: size
props.description: `sm` for a control that sits inside something else — a toolbar, a filter row, a settings line — rather than in a form of its own. It exists because every hand-written select in all three apps was the small one, and the kit only had the large one. A part is not reusable if reaching for it costs a size somebody chose on purpose.

props.name: labelHidden
props.description: Hides the label visually but keeps it for assistive tech. For fields whose surrounding row already names them — dropping the label entirely would leave the control with no accessible name at all.

name: GoogleButton
summary: Sign in with Google, in Google's own clothes.

props.name: disabled
props.description: Greyed out and unclickable while a sign-in is already in flight. A real prop rather than a fallthrough attribute: the button needs to look disabled as well as be it, and a bare `disabled` landing on the element by itself gets the second half only.

name: InstallPrompt
summary: The card that offers to install the app, and remembers being turned down.

props.name: storageKey
props.description: Where the dismissal is remembered. Namespace it: `hibi-install-nudge`.

props.name: action
props.description: The install button. Not shown on iOS, which has no API to call.

props.name: iosTitle
props.description: Shown instead of `title` where the user has to use the Share menu.

name: InstallSettings
summary: The way back to installing after the card has been dismissed.

props.name: title
props.description: The group's heading.

props.name: label
props.description: The row's label while installing is still possible.

props.name: installedLabel
props.description: The row's label once it is installed.

props.name: iosBody
props.description: Shown instead of `body` on iOS, where the user must use the Share menu.

props.name: action
props.description: The install button. Absent on iOS, which has no API to call.

name: LocaleLinks
summary: A flat language switcher for screens with no Settings behind them.

props.name: labels
props.description: Endonyms, e.g. `{ en: 'English', tr: 'Türkçe' }`.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the group.

name: LocaleSheet
summary: Choosing the interface language, from a settings row.

props.name: label
props.description: The settings row's label, and the sheet's title.

props.name: systemLabel
props.description: What "follow the device" is called. Its value is `system`.

props.name: options
props.description: In the order they should be listed. Labels are endonyms.

name: NavLinks
summary: The primary navigation of a wide site.

props.name: active
props.description: Which item is current. Usually derived from the route.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the navigation landmark.

name: OfflineBanner
summary: A floating note that the connection has gone.

props.name: label
props.description: The message. Required, because the kit has no language of its own.

name: PageContainer
summary: One measure, centred, with the page's gutters.

props.name: width
props.description: `wide` for a page, `reading` for prose, `full` to opt out.

props.name: as
props.description: The element to render. `main`, `section` and `article` all belong here.

name: PageHeader
summary: The bar at the top of a screen: a title with room either side of it.

name: PriceCard
summary: One plan in a pricing table.

props.name: price
props.description: Already formatted, or whatever stands in while there is no price.

props.name: badge
props.description: Rides on the card's edge, e.g. "Recommended".

props.name: chip
props.description: Sits inside, e.g. "30% cheaper" or "Your plan".

props.name: recommended
props.description: Raises the card and lets the badge show.

name: ProgressBar
summary: How far through something somebody is.

props.name: size
props.description: How thick the track is. `sm` for a bar under a step counter, where it is a hint rather than the subject; `lg` where the progress is the point. It shipped at one thickness and the two bars anybody wanted were `h-1`.

props.name: label
props.description: For screen readers. Without it this is a rectangle that means nothing.

name: SectionHeading
summary: A pill heading for a group of things.

props.name: count
props.description: Hidden when zero, so an empty group's heading stays quiet.

name: SegmentedControl
summary: A row of mutually exclusive choices.

name: SettingsGroup
summary: A titled run of settings rows.

name: SettingsRow
summary: One line in a settings card.

props.name: interactive
props.description: Renders the row as a button with a chevron.

props.name: stacked
props.description: Puts the control on its own line below the label, for wide controls.

name: SkeletonList
summary: A length starts with a digit, a dot, or opens a CSS function.

props.name: rowHeight
props.description: How tall each row is, as either a utility class (`h-20`) or a CSS length (`5rem`, `72px`, `var(--row)`). Both are accepted because the class-only version failed silently: a length passed here landed in `class` as `5rem`, which is not a class, so the rows had no height and the placeholder rendered as nothing at all. A loading state that shows an empty page is worse than no loading state, because it looks like the page is finished and empty.

name: StatCard
summary: One number, with what it means and which way it is going.

name: TabBar
summary: The floating bottom bar.

props.name: active
props.description: Which item is current. Usually from `route.meta`.

props.name: label
props.description: Accessible name for the navigation landmark.

name: TabShell
summary: The phone frame the whole app sits inside.

name: ToastHost
summary: Where the toasts land. One of these, at the app root.

props.name: closeLabel
props.description: The accessible name of each dismiss button. Required, because the button is an X and an X has no name — and the kit does not know the language.

props.name: bottom
props.description: Stack from the bottom instead of the top. For a phone shell, where the top is a status bar and a header and the thumb is nowhere near it.

name: ToneDot
summary: A small coloured dot, optionally labelled.

props.name: fill
props.description: Background utility for the dot, e.g. `bg-positive`.

props.name: label
props.description: Optional text after the dot. Omit for a bare marker.

name: TourShell
summary: The frame an onboarding guide runs inside.

props.name: index
props.description: Which slide, zero-based.

props.name: dialogLabel
props.description: The dialog's accessible name.

props.name: lastLabel
props.description: The button on the final slide — "Start", rather than "Next".

props.name: stepLabel
props.description: Names one segment for a screen reader, e.g. `(n) => \`Step ${n} of ${total}\``.

props.name: teleportTo
props.description: Where the dialog goes. A phone shell clips its children, so the guide has to leave the tree to cover the tab bar and the header alike.

name: UpdatePrompt
summary: The card that says a new version is waiting.

props.name: dismissLabel
props.description: The X's accessible name. An X on its own has none.
